item.text: The script fails before receiving data: its URL points to `api.weather.invalid`, so DNS returns `ENOTFOUND`. It also prints the API key in the request URL. I’m checking the project’s configuration to determine the intended provider and make the output safe.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc "node -e 'fetch(\"https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=59.437&longitude=24.7536&current=temperature_2m,relative_humidity_2m,apparent_temperature,precipitation,weather_code,wind_speed_10m&timezone=Europe%2FTallinn\").then(async r => { console.log(\"status\", r.status); const d=await r.json(); console.log(\"current fields\", Object.keys(d.current||{}).join(\",\")); }).catch(e => { console.error(e.cause?.code || e.message); process.exitCode=1; })'"

item.text: There’s no provider URL or widget code in this repo; the weather script is the only weather implementation. I’ll use Open-Meteo’s public current-conditions API for Tallinn, remove the key from request logging, and make HTTP errors visible.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc 'git diff --check && git diff -- src/weather.js && git status --short'
/bin/bash -lc 'git diff --check && git diff -- src/weather.js && git status --short'

item.text:
`npm run weather` failed because the script called `api.weather.invalid`, which returned `ENOTFOUND`. I updated [src/weather.js](/home/node/shop-api/src/weather.js) to fetch current conditions for Tallinn from Open-Meteo, report service errors, and stop printing the API key. I also removed the unused `.env` dependency from [package.json](/home/node/shop-api/package.json).

Verified: `npm run weather` now exits successfully and prints current weather data.
